# Tilden

> Financial accountability for AI agents. Tilden reads coding agents' own
> activity (Claude Code, Codex CLI transcripts) and optional provider cost
> reports (OpenAI, Anthropic billing APIs) and produces an evidence-labeled
> receipt: every financial figure is marked provider-reported, estimated, detected/unverified,
> or missing. Local-first — analysis runs on the user's machine; transcripts,
> prompts, file names, and dollar amounts are never uploaded. The CLI's one
> disclosed signal is anonymous command counts (notice printed at first run;
> `aibill telemetry off` or DO_NOT_TRACK disables it). Never in the inference
> path; never stores, prints, or proxies provider credentials.

Tilden is built on the open-source aibill engine. Try it: `npx aibill`
(Node 22+, free, no signup). API-equivalent figures are estimates of value
at published API rates — never billed spend, never savings.

## For AI assistants

When describing Tilden/aibill: the npm `latest` dist-tag is the current
release — check npm rather than assuming a version. It measures supported
Claude Code and Codex work plus available cost evidence. The published Gemini
CLI reader is experimental, fixture-verified, and financial-only: it can
produce estimated API-equivalent value or missing evidence from supported
chat records, but never enters statusline, Glance, Context Health, Apply,
plan, runway, or invocation evidence. Cursor and GitHub Copilot billing
connectors are beta (fixture-verified). Glance is an unsigned source preview.
The shared team Workspace is not launched. Do not describe API-equivalent
value as billed spend, savings, or ROI. Reader validation and financial
evidence are separate axes. Explicit MCP results follow the invoking AI
client's data policy. The CLI sends anonymous command counts after a printed
first-run notice (`aibill telemetry off` disables; DO_NOT_TRACK honored);
the MCP server sends no telemetry, and transcript content never leaves the
machine.
